notes: Every entry is a pointer: repository URL plus the exact commit the lane checks out. No third-party source is committed to this repository.
The lane clones into an ignored scratch directory, runs the scanner and codemod over the working copy, and deletes the checkout.
The lane is static analysis only. It reads source files; it never issues a request to an ArcGIS service, a portal, or a basemap.
The lane never runs `npm install` inside a cloned app, so no third-party dependency tree is ever resolved or executed.
Licenses are re-reviewed whenever a pin is moved. Only the SPDX ids in licensePolicy.allowedSpdxIds are accepted.

licensePolicy.review: Each pin records the SPDX id GitHub's license endpoint reports for the repository, a permalink to the license file, and the copyright holder named in that file. Repositories with no license, NOASSERTION, or a copyleft license are not eligible.

apps.title: CMV — Configurable Map Viewer

license.holder: David Spriggs and the CMV contributors

provenance.author: The Configurable Map Viewer community project
provenance.description: A long-running community-maintained configurable ArcGIS JS 3.x viewer built on Dojo `dijit` widgets. Local governments deploy it as-is with a JSON config; it is the single most representative example of the legacy AMD viewer a migrating team actually owns.

apps.notes: ArcGIS JS 3.37 loaded from js.arcgis.com; ~40 Dojo dijit widgets under viewer/js/gis/dijit. `viewer/js` excludes the vendored Dojo build output at the repository root.

apps.title: WSDOT Bridge Vertical Clearance

license.holder: Washington State Department of Transportation (public-domain dedication)

provenance.author: Washington State Department of Transportation, GIS Office
provenance.description: A production state-DOT lookup tool that lets freight operators find bridge vertical clearances along a route. Classic ArcGIS JS 3.25 with `esri/map`, `esri/layers/FeatureLayer`, `esri/tasks/query`, and `esri/dijit` widgets, written in TypeScript against `@types/arcgis-js-api`.

apps.notes: Repository is archived, so the pin is stable. Bare `esri/*` module specifiers resolved by the Dojo AMD loader — the hardest input shape for an ES-module-oriented codemod.

apps.title: National Park Visits explorer

license.holder: Kristian Ekenes (repository owner; unmodified Apache-2.0 text)

provenance.author: Kristian Ekenes
provenance.description: A time-series visualization of US National Park visitation built on the ArcGIS JS 4.23 AMD build. Uses the TypeScript `import X = require("esri/...")` form plus Legend, Slider, Feature, and Expand widgets — the transitional 4.x-on-AMD shape many teams are still stuck in.

apps.notes: The repository commits compiled `.js` alongside its `.ts` sources, so call-site counts include both the source and its build output. Ratios are unaffected — each construct is classified identically in both copies.

apps.title: Utah statewide parcel viewer

provenance.author: Utah Geospatial Resource Center (UGRC)
provenance.description: The public statewide parcel viewer operated by Utah's state geospatial office. React + TypeScript over `@arcgis/core` with the imperative `new EsriMap()` / `new MapView({ container })` pattern and a `FeatureLayer` per county dataset.

apps.notes: Actively developed — the pin will drift from `main`. The purest ES-module FeatureLayer target in the corpus.

apps.title: Utah Bikeways / WFRC bike map

provenance.author: Utah Geospatial Resource Center (UGRC) with the Wasatch Front Regional Council
provenance.description: A public bikeway finder for the Wasatch Front. `@arcgis/core` `WebMap` + `MapView` with BasemapToggle, Home, and Track widgets, plus `@arcgis/map-components` custom elements — the modern Esri stack a 2026 migration actually meets.

apps.notes: Mixes classic `@arcgis/core/widgets/*` imports with `@arcgis/map-components` web components; the web-component half is deliberately outside codemod scope and shows up as unhandled module hits.

apps.title: Owls of Bavaria

provenance.author: Lucia Johnson
provenance.description: A citizen-science map of owl sightings in Bavaria sourced from iNaturalist. Small React + Redux + Vite app over `@arcgis/core` using `Map`, `MapView`, `FeatureLayer`, `GeoJSONLayer`, `Graphic`, and client-side `FeatureFilter` / `FeatureEffect`.

apps.notes: The smallest app in the corpus and the fastest end-to-end smoke target; exercises the layer-support modules (`layers/support/FeatureFilter`, `FeatureEffect`) that sit next to codemod scope.
